description: PSA (Purposeful Skincare by Allies) is the affordable sister line of Allies of Skin, launched in March 2020 by founder Nicolas Travis and aimed at Gen Z and millennial shoppers, selling numbered-routine cleansers, toners, serums, night oils and creams built around actives such as mandelic acid, vitamin C and bakuchiol, through its own store and retailers including Sephora Asia, Beauty Bay and ASOS.

evidence.summary: PSA's official affiliates page states the standard offer is 15% commission (higher for larger affiliates), up to 25% via Shopify Collabs and 10-20% via Impact, and states verbatim: 'We don't believe in limiting potential... All commissions are uncapped.'

The same official page publishes hello@psaskincare.group as the contact for affiliate questions and routes sign-ups through Shopify Collabs, LTK (for individual influencers) or Impact (for publishers), with a 30-day cookie window.

Women's Weekly (Singapore) describes PSA as an offshoot of home-grown cult brand Allies of Skin, launched March 2020 as a Gen-Z and millennial-focused line with pocket-friendly prices, distributed via Sephora Malaysia/Thailand/Hong Kong, Beauty Bay and Beautylish.

Simple Life Reviews' roundup notes independent first-hand coverage of PSA is thin — a Women's Health UK whole-range write-up from November 2020 and one InStyle partnerships piece from December 2025 — indicating a small creator/review footprint relative to its parent brand.

name: PSA Skincare

opportunity.title: PSA Skincare Affiliate Program (Shopify Collabs / LTK / Impact)

reasons.compensation: Published rates on the brand's own page — 15% standard, up to 25% on Shopify Collabs, 10-20% on Impact — with commissions explicitly stated as uncapped.
reasons.contact_access: A published affiliate contact email (hello@psaskincare.group) on the official program page plus three platform sign-up routes — top band per the rubric.
reasons.credibility: Sister brand of Allies of Skin with Sephora Asia and major e-tailer distribution since its March 2020 launch.
reasons.niche_fit: Actives-led skincare aimed at Gen Z/millennial routine builders — squarely in the skincare UGC niche.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open sign-up today through Shopify Collabs, LTK or Impact, with the brand inviting affiliates to reach out directly.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A structured multi-platform affiliate program actively recruiting influencers and publishers, though independent creator coverage of the brand is still thin.

description: Toronto skincare brand founded by Thomas Tullo, founder of AMAN Spa in Toronto, selling biocellulose and hydrogel sheet masks (the Reformer Face Mask and Under-Eye Mask, formulated with NAD+, NMN and creatine) and facial tools, positioned around natural facial sculpting.

evidence.summary: Face Pilates' official Partner Program page states partners earn 5% to 15% per product sale by tier and states verbatim: 'No caps, no minimum order thresholds — every product order your content drives counts.'

The page says the program is 'Now accepting Fire Starter creators and spa professionals', pitches the brand as one 'your followers have not seen a hundred times already', sets a low 3,000-follower minimum for creators, and gives every partner a welcome kit with monthly content deliverables by tier.

The page's brand details describe Face Pilates as a Toronto skincare brand founded by Thomas Tullo (founder of AMAN Spa in Toronto) making biocellulose and hydrogel sheet masks and facial tools, with coverage in ELLE Canada, FASHION, Toronto Star and CTV.

name: Face Pilates

reasons.compensation: Published tiered rates of 5-15% per sale on the brand's own page with commissions explicitly uncapped, though entry tier starts at 5%.
reasons.contact_access: A full application form on the official page with personal review and a reply promised within five business days, but no published email.
reasons.credibility: New Toronto brand with national press/TV coverage listed on its own page and two independent consumer studies behind its masks, but a short track record.
reasons.niche_fit: Skincare masks and facial-sculpting tools built for routine content — strong fit for skincare and beauty creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Applications are open now for the entry Fire Starter tier, with a low 3,000-follower minimum for creators and no minimum for spa professionals.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A structured creator program with defined monthly deliverables, welcome kits and quarterly tier reviews, currently recruiting its first creator tiers.

description: Online-only luxury cosmetics brand selling clean, vegan makeup (its ColorEccentric line) made with European and American craftsmanship, sold exclusively through its own platform and promoted through a small, selective network of Envoy partners rather than retail stores.

evidence.summary: Only1's Envoy Program listing states a 25% commission on beauty purchases and referrals for the lifetime of the partnership, paid weekly, and states verbatim: 'Earn 25% commissions for life—no cap on your potential.'

The same listing invites applicants to 'Get in on the ground floor of an exciting cosmetics company as one of our first 25 specially selected Envoy Partners' — direct evidence the creator program is brand new and capped at a first cohort of 25.

The listing describes Only1 as an online-only luxury beauty brand with clean vegan formulas, and requires Envoys to have B2C sales or retail beauty experience plus engaged beauty/skincare social followings.

name: Only1

reasons.compensation: 25% commission for the lifetime of the partnership with weekly payouts and an explicit 'no cap on your potential' statement — among the strongest published offers in this batch.
reasons.contact_access: A live application listing, but no published email or open program page on the brand's own site — mid-range per the rubric.
reasons.credibility: New online-only luxury brand built by beauty-industry insiders, but with little independent track record so far.
reasons.niche_fit: Luxury vegan makeup built entirely around influencer and ambassador selling — a core beauty UGC niche.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Applications are open, but the program is highly selective (first 25 Envoys) and asks for prior sales or retail beauty experience.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A dedicated Envoy program for beauty influencers with mentorship, marketing support and a toolkit, currently recruiting its first cohort.

description: Professional haircare brand with a protein-free, hydration-focused product line, sold through salons and its own store, whose affiliate program is built specifically for licensed stylists, suite owners and salon teams rather than the general influencer market.

evidence.summary: Goldie Locks' official Pro Affiliate Program page publishes tiered commissions — 10% (Insider), 15% (Muse), 20% (Star), 25% (Icon) by total sales — and lists 'Unlimited earning potential' among the program details.

The same page restricts the program to licensed professional stylists, suite owners, salon teams and assistants building clientele — a deliberately small, professional-only creator pool rather than an open influencer program.

name: Goldie Locks

reasons.compensation: Published tiered rates rising from 10% to 25% with 'Unlimited earning potential' stated on the brand's own program page.
reasons.contact_access: A dedicated pro program page with a join route, but no published partnerships email — mid-range per the rubric.
reasons.credibility: Established professional haircare brand sold through salons with brand-backed education and support for affiliates.
reasons.niche_fit: Haircare is a core beauty niche, though the program targets working stylists more than general UGC creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open to join for licensed stylists and salon professionals; general creators without a license are out of scope.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A formal affiliate program with tier progression and brand education, aimed at professionals who already recommend products to clients.

description: Botanical beauty brand selling pure, organic and wildcrafted oils, essences and extracts for skin, body and oral care — its 'liquid libations' formulations are synthetic-free, food-grade and microbiome-friendly, sold through its own store and a store-locator retail network.

evidence.summary: Living Libations' official affiliates page offers 'Renegade Beauty Affiliates' an introductory 8% commission rate with room to grow, bonuses and giveaways, and states verbatim: 'With no cap on your potential and monthly payouts, your passion becomes your prosperity.'

The same page publishes Affiliate@LivingLibations.com for the program and requires applicants to submit a partnership application and promotion plan for review before receiving a tracking link — a small, curated program rather than instant open enrollment.

name: Living Libations

opportunity.title: Living Libations Renegade Beauty Affiliate Program

reasons.compensation: A published 8% introductory rate with performance growth and an explicit no-cap statement, but the starting rate is modest.
reasons.contact_access: A published affiliate email plus an application route on the official page — near top band per the rubric.
reasons.credibility: Long-running botanical beauty brand with its own retail store-locator network and a loyal niche following.
reasons.niche_fit: Botanical skincare and beauty oils with a devoted clean-beauty audience — strong UGC niche fit.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Applications are open, subject to a manual review of the applicant's promotion plan.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A named affiliate community ('Renegade Beauty Affiliates') with creative assets, launch previews and education, kept small by application review.

description: Small herbal skincare brand selling natural skin care products, organic bath and body care and herbal remedies through its own website, running a long-standing in-house affiliate program aimed at website owners rather than social influencers.

evidence.summary: Alchemilla's official affiliate page lists 15% tier-1 commission plus 2% tier-2, a 365-day cookie and a $10 payout threshold, and its FAQ answers 'Are there limits to how much I can earn?' with: 'The sky is the limit! There is no limit to the amount of commission you can earn.'

The same page shows the program has run in-house since January 31, 2012 with manual application review and link-based tracking — a small, website-focused program with no influencer or ambassador layer.

name: Alchemilla

reasons.compensation: Published 15% tier-1 plus 2% tier-2 commission with a 365-day cookie and an explicit 'no limit' statement on the brand's own page.
reasons.contact_access: A public sign-up form and contact route on the official program page, but no published partnerships email — mid-range per the rubric.
reasons.credibility: Small herbal brand whose affiliate program has operated since 2012, but with a modest public footprint.
reasons.niche_fit: Natural and herbal skincare fits the clean-beauty UGC niche, though the program is oriented to websites over social creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free to join with an online application and manual approval — open today.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A real, long-running affiliate program, but built on website links rather than creator content, so UGC-specific evidence is limited.

description: Indie organic skincare brand founded by Cassandra Dailey, selling natural, earth-based skincare and wellness products through its own website, with a sustainability and indigenous-causes mission and a founder-led affiliate community.

evidence.summary: BFree Organics' official affiliate page promises affiliates their own discount code and states verbatim: 'Earn Residual Income: Gain commissions on every sale with no cap on your earnings.' No percentage rate is published on the page.

The same page runs applications through a simple form, offers monthly perks and direct access to founder/CEO Cassandra Dailey, and requires affiliates to stay active on social media and maintain a minimum sales threshold — a small, hands-on indie program.

name: BFree Organics

reasons.compensation: Commissions on every sale with an explicit no-cap statement, but no published percentage rate, so this stays low per the rubric.
reasons.contact_access: A public application form linked from the official program page, but no published email — mid-range per the rubric.
reasons.credibility: Small founder-led indie brand with a sustainability mission; limited independent coverage.
reasons.niche_fit: Organic, earth-based skincare — a clear clean-beauty UGC niche fit.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Applications are open now via the form linked on the official page.
reasons.ugc_evidence: An active affiliate community with monthly perks, product bonuses and founder access, run at indie scale.

description: Small clean-skincare brand whose products are handmade in small batches with organic ingredients — its range centers on whipped tallow balms (Soothe, Clear, Plump and Basics) made from grass-fed tallow with plant oils, sold through its own website.

evidence.summary: OG GLOW's official affiliate program page (run on BixGrow) states verbatim: 'Unlimited Earning Potential: The more you promote, the more you earn - no cap on commissions, so you control your income', with a 30-day cookie and monthly payout at a $25 minimum. No percentage rate is published on the page.

The same page tells affiliates 'Your support & feedback helps shape OG GLOW's future' and offers early access to new products — early-stage brand language consistent with a small, still-forming creator base.
OG GLOW's own product page describes its whipped tallow balms as 'handmade in small batches with organic ingredients', supporting the picture of a small-batch indie brand.

name: OG GLOW

reasons.compensation: An explicit no-cap statement on the official program page, but no published commission percentage, so this stays low per the rubric.
reasons.contact_access: A public sign-up form on the program page with review promised within two business days, but no published email — mid-range per the rubric.
reasons.credibility: Very small handmade-batch brand with a narrow product range and little independent coverage.
reasons.niche_fit: Tallow-based clean skincare is a trending niche on TikTok and fits skincare UGC well.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open sign-up today through the brand's BixGrow affiliate page.
reasons.ugc_evidence: An open affiliate program explicitly courting influencers and content creators, at an early stage of the brand's growth.

description: New natural skincare brand selling clean, nature-based products through its own website, recruiting content creators, beauty influencers, bloggers and loyal customers into a curated affiliate network with training resources and monthly performance bonuses.

evidence.summary: Billionaire Skincare's official affiliate page states affiliates 'Earn generous commissions on every qualified sale you refer — with no cap on your earning potential', with monthly bonuses for top performers; its FAQ says exact rates vary by tier and are provided upon approval, so no rate is published.

The same page opens applications to creators with as few as 500 followers, describes a 'curated network of creators, influencers, and skincare advocates', and promises a welcome kit, training library and a 30-day cookie — a small program still being built.

name: Billionaire Skincare

reasons.compensation: An explicit no-cap statement and monthly performance bonuses, but rates are only disclosed after approval, so this stays low per the rubric.
reasons.contact_access: A full application form on the official page with a 3-5 business day review promise, but no published email — mid-range per the rubric.
reasons.credibility: New brand with no verifiable retail distribution or independent coverage found.
reasons.niche_fit: Natural skincare aimed squarely at beauty creators and influencers — strong niche fit.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Applications are open now, including to creators with as few as 500 followers.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A creator-first affiliate program with welcome kits, training resources and launch access, described by the brand as a curated (small) network.

description: Skincare water-filtration brand founded by sisters Xin and Lynn Shui, launched in 2022 with a faucet filter designed specifically for skincare, now selling skincare faucet filters and shower filters through its own site and retailers including Amazon, Urban Outfitters, Bloomingdale's and Thirteen Lune.

evidence.summary: Filterbaby's official affiliate terms list as a program feature: 'Competitive Commission Rates – Starting at 15%* w/ no cap', with a 7-day cookie, influencer/content creator product seeding and payouts 60 days after conversion at a $19.99 minimum.

The brand's Thirteen Lune launch release reports that since its 2022 inception Filterbaby had sold nearly 100,000 units and built over half a million social followers and one billion views across Instagram, TikTok and YouTube — evidence of a large existing audience, so low creator saturation could NOT be evidenced for this brand and saturation is marked unknown.

Alpha Leaders reports Filterbaby launched in mid-2022 with $20,000 in bootstrap funding and scaled to eight figures in its second full year, winning New Beauty's 'Best Shower Filter' and a TIME Best Inventions mention.

name: Filterbaby

reasons.compensation: Published terms start affiliates at 15% with an explicit 'no cap' statement on the brand's own site.
reasons.contact_access: Program terms are public on the official site, but no dedicated partnerships email was verified — mid-range per the rubric.
reasons.credibility: Fast-growing brand with clinical testing claims, national retail distribution and major press recognition since 2022.
reasons.niche_fit: Skincare-adjacent filtration devices rather than topical skincare — a partial fit for skincare UGC.
reasons.opportunity_availability: The affiliate program is live under published terms, including creator product seeding.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The terms explicitly include influencer/content creator product seeding, and the brand was built on viral TikTok content.
